propositions: _recall_false_accept computes the fraction of safe items NOT blocked (specificity), but both consumption sites treat it as an error rate (lower-is-better), inverting the gate logic and causing competent candidates to be wrongly rejected
The max_false_accept ceiling of 0.10 effectively always fails because the old computation yields values near 1.0 for any reasonable run that does not block safe items
A candidate improving from 0.786 to 0.929 specificity (2 fewer false fires on gold-ADVISORY items) was rejected with 'false-accept rose 0.143' under the inverted metric

The repository already defines false_accept consistently elsewhere as wrongly-fired / must-not-fire (eval.py) and as a lower-is-better error metric (docs and container eval), so the parity computation is an outlier

The fix inverts the numerator in the false_accept expression to count blocked safe items instead of not-blocked safe items, leaving all comparison operators unchanged to converge with the existing codebase definition
